correctness.rationale: Exact diagonalization yields 1/delta noise singularity with uniformly Gaussian-tail remainder; signed separation integration gives the two-sided 1/t coefficient. Lipschitz evaluation cancels the deterministic collision, and dominated convergence after delta=sqrt(eta/alpha)z yields the positive pi/(4 alpha^(3/2)) coefficient. Separate deterministic numerical checks verify expressions but are not treated as universal proof.

value.rationale: Natural fixed-two-point iid random-design Bayesian quadrature under physical independent Gaussian observation noise exhibits a sharp moment catastrophe that is absent for Lipschitz noiseless data. The exact tail and 1/sqrt(nugget) constants quantify regularization burden and yield a sigma rather than sigma^2 MSE for the noise-matched choice; this is a motivated diagnostic benchmark, not an arbitrary unmotivated slice.
